"'''Loch Henry'''" is the second episode of the sixth series of the anthology series ''[[Black Mirror]]''. It was written by the series creator [[Charlie Brooker]] and directed by [[Sam Miller]]. Alongside the rest of the sixth series, it premiered on [[Netflix]] on 15 June 2023. The episode follows Davis ([[Samuel Blenkin]]) and Pia ([[Myha'la Herrold]]) as they make a [[true crime]] documentary in Davis's run-down hometown in [[Scotland]].

Brooker reflected on the cinematic style of true crime documentaries and how he and his wife had considered traveling to Scotland after seeing its depiction in a documentary. "Loch Henry" was the first episode set in Scotland, as the setting of "[[Crocodile (Black Mirror)|Crocodile]]" was changed to Iceland; 18 locations in Scotland were used for filming. The episode criticises the effects of true crime media on victims and highlights dissonant attitudes of the creators and consumers of true crime media. The episode references other ''Black Mirror'' events through newspapers and other text; its themes were compared to "[[Joan Is Awful]]", which is also about [[streaming service|streaming television]].

The episode placed around the middle of critics' lists of ''Black Mirror'' installments by quality, though most reviews aggregated by [[Rotten Tomatoes]] were positive. Reviewers wrote negatively of the episode's moral but positively about the characters and acting. Critics were ambivalent towards the plot twist.

== Plot ==
Davis McCardle ([[Samuel Blenkin]]) visits his childhood home in Loch Henry, [[Scotland]], with his American girlfriend Pia Koreshi ([[Myha'la Herrold]]). They met in a film course and are pursuing Davis's idea for a documentary about an amateur conservationist in [[Rùm]] who prevents [[oology|illegal egg collecting]]. Davis's mother Janet ([[Monica Dolan]]) cooks for them, but she and Pia are uneasy around each other.

Davis introduces Pia to his friend Stuart King ([[Daniel Portman]]), who runs the only remaining pub in Loch Henry, the Lochside Inn. Stuart's father Richard ([[John Hannah (actor)|John Hannah]]) is an alcoholic. The former tourist haven is run down because, in the 1990s, resident Iain Adair (Tom Crowhurst) made national headlines as a [[serial killer]]. Davis's policeman father Kenneth (Gregor Firth) was called to Adair's home after Adair made drunken comments about missing tourists. Adair shot his parents, Kenneth and himself. Wounded in the shoulder, Kenneth acquired [[MRSA]] in hospital and died when Davis was eight.

Pia proposes a [[true crime]] documentary about Adair. Davis is worried about its local impact, but Stuart believes the film will bring in tourism, and Janet is happy to voice her anger about Adair's responsibility for Kenneth's death. They pitch it to the producer Kate Cezar ([[Ellie White]]), who wants new information uncovered. Davis, Pia and Stuart break into Adair's abandoned home and find evidence of torture in the basement. They film footage with an old camera, taping over Janet's ''[[Bergerac (TV series)|Bergerac]]'' [[VHS]] cassettes. Returning home, they get in a car accident. Davis has to stay overnight in hospital, where Richard—recovering from a fall down the stairs—voices opposition to the documentary.

Pia discovers that Janet's cassettes contain recordings of Janet and Kenneth alongside Adair, torturing his victims. Pia flees the house, unable to get phone service. Janet realises what Pia has discovered and pursues her. Pia hits her head while fleeing through a stream in darkness and dies. Janet returns to the house, leaves a note next to evidence of her crimes, and hangs herself.

Davis assists on a Streamberry documentary about his parents' criminal activity. An interview shows that Richard suspected Janet and Kenneth's involvement after unnerving sexual activity with the couple. Kenneth killed the Adair family and wounded himself so it appeared that Iain worked alone.

Stuart is delighted as tourists fill the Lochside Inn and the series wins a [[BAFTA]] award that Cezar dedicates to Davis. After the awards ceremony, Davis returns unhappily to his hotel room and re-reads his mother's suicide note: "For your film. Mum."

that the "texture of old media" had become fetishised.<ref name="BAFTA"/>{{rp|7:45–8:00}}

Brooker was inspired by true crime documentaries, noticing how the genre's increasingly cinematic and [[art house]] style gave an air of being "somber, serious" and "important". ==Analysis==
Neil Armstrong of ''[[BBC Culture]]'' suggested the episode was the most disturbing of the sixth series;<ref name="BBC">{{cite web |last=Armstrong |first=Neil |title=Black Mirror season six review: Charlie Brooker's series is 'a show that revels in its twists' |url=https://www.bbc.com/culture/article/20230614-black-mirror-season-six-review-charlie-brookers-series-is-a-show-that-revels-in-its-twists |website=[[BBC Culture]] |date=15 June 2023 |accessdate=27 August 2023 |archive-date=20 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230720174319/https://www.bbc.com/culture/article/20230614-black-mirror-season-six-review-charlie-brookers-series-is-a-show-that-revels-in-its-twists |url-status=live }}</ref> critics identified it as a slow-paced [[mystery fiction]] with elements of [[folk horror]].<ref name="RS"/><ref name="Tele"/> The episode critiques true crime;<ref name="Paste"/><ref name="Tele"/> according to ''[[i (newspaper)|i]]''{{'}}s Emily Baker, it reveals the genre as "pointless" and "empty".<ref name="i"/> ''[[Den of Geek]]''{{'}}s Louisa Mellor wrote that it was rare for ''Black Mirror'' to give clear answers to moral questions, but that "Loch Henry" does so in its portrayal of true crime.<ref name="DoG review">{{cite web|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/black-mirror-season-6-episode-2-review-loch-henry/|title=Black Mirror Season 6 Episode 2 Review: Loch Henry|work=[[Den of Geek]]|last=Mellor|first=Louisa|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=27 August 2023|archive-date=28 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230628123512/https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/black-mirror-season-6-episode-2-review-loch-henry/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Davis, Pia and Stuart speak flippantly about Iain Adair's murders. A [[montage (filmmaking)|montage]] shows the "tonal dissonance" in their attitudes.<ref name="Verge"/> The characters get into a car crash because they are distracted by singing a comedy song about Adair torturing his victims.<ref name="i"/> Davis and Stuart are initially excited, "not disgusted or saddened", to tell Pia about the murders, according to Mellor.<ref name="DoG review"/> Pia's death can be seen as retribution for her delight in the unpleasant stories about Adair or for taking advantage of Davis's family tragedy.<ref name="DoG review"/><ref name="Vulture"/> Like characters in the ''[[Blair Witch]]'' franchise, which is referenced in dialogue, Davis investigates a story and becomes its subject.<ref name="Vulture"/>

A red [[masquerade ball|masquerade]] mask worn by Janet in the [[snuff video]] that Pia watches is a recurring symbol. Janet is seen putting it on again before hanging herself.<ref name="RT mask"/><ref name="Vulture"/> Tourists in the Lochside Inn wear similar masks as costumes.<ref name="Mashable">{{cite web|url=https://sea.mashable.com/tv-shows/24568/black-mirror-episode-loch-henry-could-have-gone-harder-on-true-crime-tourism|title='Black Mirror' episode 'Loch Henry' could have gone harder on true crime tourism|work=[[Mashable]]|last=Connellan|first=Shannon|date=27 June 2023|accessdate=25 August 2023|archive-date=26 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230826151039/https://sea.mashable.com/tv-shows/24568/black-mirror-episode-loch-henry-could-have-gone-harder-on-true-crime-tourism|url-status=live}}</ref> The episode ends with a visual of a mask, on the BAFTA award that Davis wins.<ref name="RT mask">{{cite web|url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/black-mirror-loch-henry-double-meaning-newsupdate/|title=Black Mirror actor reveals unsettling double-meaning in Loch Henry|work=[[Radio Times]]|last=Cormack|first=Morgan|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=25 August 2023|archive-date=23 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230623145128/https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/black-mirror-loch-henry-double-meaning-newsupdate/|url-status=live}}</ref> A similar recurring symbol is a butterfly pin badge worn by murder victim Dawn Challis, which is seen in a keepsake box opened by Janet just before her hanging herself. According to ''[[Vulture (magazine)|Vulture]]''{{'}}s Ben Rosenstock, the note that Janet leaves Davis is a "little sign of his mother's love", despite her sadism. Davis has to reinterpret his parents' love in light of their actions.<ref name="Vulture">{{cite web|url=https://www.vulture.com/article/black-mirror-recap-season-6-episode-two-loch-henry.html|title=''Black Mirror'' Recap: Farmicide|work=[[Vulture (magazine)|Vulture]]|last=Rosenstock|first=Ben|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=27 August 2023|archive-date=14 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230714165054/https://www.vulture.com/article/black-mirror-recap-season-6-episode-two-loch-henry.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Janet has a collection of ''Bergerac'' recordings—according to ''[[Marie Claire]]''{{'}}s Quinci LeGardye, the [[BBC]] detective series showcased "inoffensive crimes", making it an apt choice for a mother's favourite series.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marieclaire.com/culture/tv-shows/is-loch-henry-from-black-mirror-a-real-place/|title=Is Loch Henry From 'Black Mirror' A Real Place?|work=[[Marie Claire]]|last=LeGardye|first=Quinci|date=20 June 2023|accessdate=25 August 2023|archive-date=25 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230825150936/https://www.marieclaire.com/culture/tv-shows/is-loch-henry-from-black-mirror-a-real-place/|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[File:John Hannah by Gage Skidmore.jpg|thumb|upright|alt=John Hannah|Richard King is played by [[John Hannah (actor)|John Hannah]].]]
Stuart's father Richard King owns the Lochside Inn. He objects to the documentary's creation on the grounds that it is opportunistic. This is a [[red herring]] that suggests his involvement; he had additional knowledge but did not take part in criminality.<ref name="Vulture"/> Like the Lochside Inn, Shannon Connellan of ''[[Mashable]]'' noted, establishments associated with serial killers—the [[Ten Bells]], The Last Resort and [[L&L Tavern]]—attract tourism.<ref name="Mashable"/>

Comparisons to other series six episodes were made by critics. [[Streaming service]]s such as Netflix and the fictional Streamberry—both mentioned in "Loch Henry"<ref name="Mashable"/>—are also the subject of "[[Joan Is Awful]]", in which the title character's life is adapted in real-time into a television programme.<ref name="Variety"/><ref name="Time">{{cite magazine|url=https://time.com/6287513/black-mirror-season-6-review/|title=What Even Is ''Black Mirror'' Anymore?|magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]|last=Berman|first=Judy|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=23 August 2023|archive-date=15 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230715005440/https://time.com/6287513/black-mirror-season-6-review/|url-status=live}}</ref> The documentary ''Loch Henry: Truth Will Out'' can be seen on Joan's Streamberry account.<ref name="DoG egg">{{cite web|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/black-mirror-season-6-easter-eggs-upend-the-shows-shared-universe/|title=Black Mirror Season 6 Easter Eggs Upend the Show's Shared Universe|work=[[Den of Geek]]|last=Bojalad|first=Alec|last2=Mellor|first2=Louisa|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=23 August 2023|archive-date=20 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230720212347/https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/black-mirror-season-6-easter-eggs-upend-the-shows-shared-universe/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="DoG reverse">{{cite web|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/why-you-should-watch-black-mirror-season-6-in-reverse-order/|title=Why You Should Watch Black Mirror Season 6 in Reverse Order|work=[[Den of Geek]]|last=Harrisson|first=Juliette|date=21 June 2023|accessdate=23 August 2023|archive-date=3 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230703084812/https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/why-you-should-watch-black-mirror-season-6-in-reverse-order/|url-status=live}}</ref> "Loch Henry", like "[[Mazey Day (Black Mirror)|Mazey Day]]", criticises [[mass media]] and sees inquisitive characters led into danger by their profession.<ref name="Time"/><ref name="Variety">{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2023/tv/reviews/black-mirror-season-6-review-1235644259/|title='Black Mirror' Season 6 Is a Refreshingly Uncynical Return to Form: TV Review|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|last=D'Addario|first=Daniel|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=23 August 2023|archive-date=25 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230625033800/https://variety.com/2023/tv/reviews/black-mirror-season-6-review-1235644259/|url-status=live}}</ref> Pia is subject to racism, a central theme of "Demon 79".<ref name="DoG reverse"/> The episode was also seen as thematically similar to series one's "Fifteen Million Merits", which shows [[commodification]] and [[talent show]] television impacting human empathy.<ref name="DoG review"/>

Additionally, the episode makes [[Easter egg (media)|Easter egg]] references to other ''Black Mirror'' events through newspapers, [[news ticker]]s and BAFTA-nominated documentaries. Referenced events include: Michael Smart of "[[Demon 79]]" launching his new political party; Cooper of "[[Playtest (Black Mirror)|Playtest]]" being found dead; auditions for the "[[Fifteen Million Merits]]" talent show ''Hot Shots'' opening in Australia; and a [[The Waldo Moment|Waldo]] sticker on Davis's computer. The two documentaries competing with Davis's Loch Henry production for a [[Bafta]] are Suffer the Children: The Tipley Paedophile Ring and Euthanasia: Inside Project Junipero. Tipley is the fictional town from the episode [[Demon 79]], and Project Junipero is in reference to the episode [[San Junipero]]. Brooker highlighted as a favourite that Michael Callow of "[[The National Anthem (Black Mirror)|The National Anthem]]" is said to run a zoo.<ref name="DoG egg"/>

== Reception ==
On the review aggregator [[Rotten Tomatoes]], the episode holds an approval rating of 87% based on 15 reviews.<ref>{{cite Rotten Tomatoes |type=tv |id=black_mirror |season=6 |episode=2 |access-date=22 June 2023}}</ref> Out of five stars, it was rated four stars by ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]'', ''Vulture'' and ''i'',<ref name="Tele"/><ref name="Vulture"/><ref name="i"/> 3.5 stars by ''Den of Geek'',<ref name="DoG review"/> and three stars by ''[[The Independent]]''.<ref name="Indy"/> The "delicious sense of impending doom" and "pleasing wicked streak" of the episode were praised by ''[[The A.V. Club]]''{{'}}s Kayleigh Dray and ''[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]''{{'}}s Richard Lawson, respectively.<ref name="AVClub">{{cite web|url=https://www.avclub.com/black-mirror-season-6-tv-review-netflix-charlie-brooker-1850540964|title=''Black Mirror'' season 6 review: Through the past, darkly|work=[[The A.V. Club]]|last=Dray|first=Kayleigh|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=27 August 2023|archive-date=20 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230720184040/https://www.avclub.com/black-mirror-season-6-tv-review-netflix-charlie-brooker-1850540964|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Vanity Fair">{{cite web|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2023/06/black-mirror-season-6-review|title=''Black Mirror''{{'}}s Odd Future Feels Stuck in the Past|work=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]|last=Lawson|first=Richard|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=27 August 2023|archive-date=20 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230620063648/https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2023/06/black-mirror-season-6-review|url-status=live}}</ref> Lawson summarised it a "predictable but compelling thriller" that explored the themes of "Joan Is Awful" more successfully.<ref name="Vanity Fair"/> Rosenstock found that it told a "complete, purposeful story" with natural [[exposition (narrative)|exposition]];<ref name="Vulture"/> [[Alan Sepinwall]], writing in ''[[Rolling Stone]]'', found it well-paced, except for a rushed ending.<ref name="RS">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-reviews/black-mirror-season-6-review-mocks-netflix-annie-murphy-salma-hayek-1234770401/|title='Black Mirror' Season Six Takes Aim at Netflix But Feels Stuck in the Past|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|last=Sepinwall|first=Alan|author-link=Alan Sepinwall|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=27 August 2023}}</ref>

The episode's message received criticism. In ''The Independent'', Nick Hilton summarised it as "vague, underlying commentary on the commercialisation of tragedy".<ref name="Indy">{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/reviews/black-mirror-season-6-review-episodes-ranked-b2357292.html|title=Black Mirror season six review: Charlie Brooker's sci-fi mishmash needs to stop messing with a winning formula|work=[[The Independent]]|last=Hilton|first=Nick|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=27 August 2023|archive-date=16 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230616020939/https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/reviews/black-mirror-season-6-review-episodes-ranked-b2357292.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Rachel Dodes of ''[[Esquire (magazine)|Esquire]]'' found it guilty of the "torture porn" that it attempts to criticise; Lawson did not believe its message was original.<ref name="Esquire">{{cite web|url=https://www.esquire.com/entertainment/tv/a44215185/black-mirror-season-6-review/|title=''Black Mirror'' Season 6: Every Episode, Reviewed|work=[[Esquire (magazine)|Esquire]]|last=Dodes|first=Rachel|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=27 August 2023|archive-date=14 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230714071141/https://www.esquire.com/entertainment/tv/a44215185/black-mirror-season-6-review/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Vanity Fair"/> Adi Robertson wrote for ''[[The Verge]]'' that it makes "fairly mild observations" about true crime, but fans of the genre already understand its moral issues. She said it failed to explore "the potential ugliness of its premise" or create "characters who transcend it".<ref name="Verge">{{cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/2023/6/16/23763257/black-mirror-season-6-loch-henry-true-crime-review-netflix|title=Black Mirror's 'Loch Henry' can't decide whether to indulge in true crime or critique it|work=[[The Verge]]|last=Robertson|first=Adi|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=27 August 2023|archive-date=15 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230715085603/https://www.theverge.com/2023/6/16/23763257/black-mirror-season-6-loch-henry-true-crime-review-netflix|url-status=live}}</ref> Connellan was incredulous that Loch Henry would not have attracted true crime tourism before Davis's documentary. She suggested the episode could have further depicted the insensitivity of such tourism.<ref name="Mashable"/>

The [[plot twist]] and ending was met with mixed feedback. Despite finding the twist predictable, ''[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]''{{'}}s Leila Jordan lauded the "great ''Black Mirror'' gut punch at the end".<ref name="Paste">{{cite web|url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/tv/netflix/black-mirror-season-6-review|title=''Black Mirror'' Struggles to Imagine the Future in an Uneven Season 6|work=[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]|last=Jordan|first=Leila|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=27 August 2023|archive-date=24 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230724170744/https://www.pastemagazine.com/tv/netflix/black-mirror-season-6-review|url-status=live}}</ref> In contrast, Robertson believed the "deliberately unsatisfying" conclusion was "rushed" and inferior to the plot twist of "[[White Bear (Black Mirror)|White Bear]]".<ref name="Verge"/> Baker was surprised by the twist, but experienced a "frustrating wait" for it.<ref name="i"/> The "sad and empty" conclusion was criticised by Dodes.<ref name="Esquire"/> Rosenstock, in contrast, praised its focus on "psychological implications" for Davis rather than "cultural commentary", making it a "fascinating, haunting ending".<ref name="Vulture"/>

The acting and characterisation was widely praised. Hilton reviewed that the "sterling" cast "bring an increasing sense of unease" to the episode.<ref name="Indy"/> Rosenstock praised the "nice chemistry" from "Stuart's brashness", "Davis's tentativeness" and "Pia's adventurous attitude", as well as these characters' humour. He found that Pia's greedy side "doesn't go too far" and lauded Herrold's performance of Pia's "horror and disbelief" at the snuff video and "barely concealed fear" in front of Janet.<ref name="Vulture"/> Ed Power, writing in ''The Daily Telegraph'', similarly praised Pia's portrayal as "an outwardly kind person with an inner core that's all ambition" and said Blenkin "shines in the final moments" of the story.<ref name="Tele">{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/tv/2023/06/15/black-mirror-season-6-e2-review-loch-henry/|title=In Loch Henry, Black Mirror takes on relentless and exploitative true-crime|work=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|last=Power|first=Ed|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=27 August 2023|archive-date=7 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230707025506/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/tv/2023/06/15/black-mirror-season-6-e2-review-loch-henry/|url-status=live}}</ref> For Baker, the episode's highlights were Stuart's "gruff but likeable personality and hilarious quips".<ref name="i"/> However, Robertson critiqued that Davis lacks "a strong enough presence" for his "familial drama" to have emotional impact.<ref name="Verge"/>

Dolan's role as Janet was also praised. Power found that she "captures the duality of a person with dark depths".<ref name="Tele"/> Rosenstock said that Dolan manages to give "weird vibes from the beginning" that make sense from a "lonely, grief-stricken widow" but suggest something deeper.<ref name="Vulture"/> Though calling Dolan "excellent", Baker criticised her Scottish accent.<ref name="i"/>

* 15th – Lucy Ford, Jack King and Brit Dawson, ''[[GQ]]''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gq-magazine.co.uk/article/all-28-black-mirror-episodes-ranked|title=All 28 ''Black Mirror'' episodes (including season 6), ranked|work=[[GQ]]|last1=Ford|first1=Lucy|last2=King|first2=Jack|last3=Dawson|first3=Brit|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=22 August 2023|archive-date=24 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230724134847/https://www.gq-magazine.co.uk/article/all-28-black-mirror-episodes-ranked|url-status=live}}</ref>

* 16th – Ed Power, ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/on-demand/0/black-mirror-best-episodes-worst-ranked/|title=Black Mirror: every episode, ranked from best to worst|work=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|last=Power|first=Ed|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=22 August 2023|archive-date=15 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210115155347/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/on-demand/0/black-mirror-best-episodes-worst-ranked/|url-status=live}}</ref>

''[[IndieWire]]'' and ''[[GamesRadar+]]'' listed the 27 episodes, excluding ''Bandersnatch'', where "Loch Henry" placed 13th and 25th, respectively.<ref name="GamesRadar ranking">{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/best-black-mirror-episodes/|title=All Black Mirror episodes ranked, from Be Right Back to Beyond the Sea|work=[[GamesRadar+]]|last=West|first=Amy|date=23 June 2023|accessdate=22 August 2023|archive-date=30 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230630173026/https://www.gamesradar.com/best-black-mirror-episodes/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.indiewire.com/features/best-of/best-black-mirror-episodes-worst-netflix-ranked-1201897973/|title=Every 'Black Mirror' Episode, Ranked|work=[[IndieWire]]|last1=Greene|first1=Steve|last2=Khosla|first2=Proma|date=20 June 2023|accessdate=22 August 2023|archive-date=2 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230702125946/https://www.indiewire.com/features/best-of/best-black-mirror-episodes-worst-netflix-ranked-1201897973/|url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[The New York Observer]]'' described it as the second-best of the five episodes in series six.<ref name="Observer">{{cite web|url=https://observer.com/2023/06/black-mirror-season-6-review-ranking-the-new-episodes-from-best-to-worst/|title='Black Mirror' Season 6 Review: Ranking the New Episodes from Best to Worst|work=[[The New York Observer]]|last=Babiak|first=Laura|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=3 August 2023|archive-date=20 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230620151707/https://observer.com/2023/06/black-mirror-season-6-review-ranking-the-new-episodes-from-best-to-worst/|url-status=live}}</ref>
